analysis.title: International Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing (Nov 12, 2026)
key_insights: Tech rally is wavering, weighed by reports NVDA is preparing to oust its CEO. The divergence versus NDX has been notable. As of yesterday, SOX was flat versus its pre-midterm level.
Broadening continues to stand out, with EU futures higher this morning. US bond markets return from the Veterans Day holiday, and the day is busy for Fed speakers.

Signs of capitulation (largest unwind of momentum (MOMO) in ~40 years, deleveraging metrics back at Liberation Day levels, a very bearish sentiment shift) plus year-end seasonality supported JPM's view for a MOMO longs bounce, which has started to play out.

Positioning Intelligence saw investors closing gaps and neutralizing risk after the midterms via short covering rather than chasing, so there is still room for risk to be added back. Retail remains a key support, with strong equity and leveraged ETF buying.

Nikos attributes the post-midterm drawdown to leveraged equity ETF rebalancing, vol-induced de-risking by risk parity funds, and MOMO-based investors capitulating and turning short. HF de-risking also shows in QQQ short interest rising to its highest since 2023.

EU is among the broadening outperformers, helped by an improved geopolitical narrative after the US midterms across the Middle East and Russia/Ukraine. Zelenskyy said political shifts open a window for Russia talks. SX5E futures positioning is at a 12-month high at +2.9z, driven by short covering.
Energy is the key risk for Europe. EU LNG imports lag last year's levels, unusually low winter stockpiles have started to fall, and the Iran war removes about one fifth of global LNG exports.

USDJPY is nearing 160 for the first time since early September, prompting intervention warnings. JPM published a deep-dive on yen flows. Japanese sovereign debt investors reallocated within Europe in September, shifting out of France into Germany and the UK.

Copper has been range-bound for three months between about $14,000 and $14,800/t. US tariff threats linger and sentiment has tilted to cautious uncertainty. Global and US PMIs remain strong at 52.6 and 54.9 despite the faltering AI trade. US inventory draws are creating physical tightness in the rest of the world, weak Chilean mine output adds to it, and China cathode premia have spiked. LME speculative positioning has fallen materially and forward pricing sits below spot through next year.

Yen FX flows: since the LDP leadership election last October the yen has weakened across G10 currencies, yet balance-of-payments-related FX flows show record net yen buying, partly from ¥27 trillion ($170 billion) of yen-buying intervention.

Market Intelligence is tactically bullish on global equities. Regional preference stays long US and Asia (Japan, South Korea, Taiwan) versus EU, as the US is overheating, Europe is recovering from stagflation, and Asia has pockets of both. Broadening can return, more clearly in the US than in the EU, and EU conviction needs stability in EGB spreads.

Positioning Intelligence weekly wrap: Multi-Strat alpha and HF returns are likely to recover but uncertainty persists. After the largest 20-day Multi-Strat de-grossing since Covid, long-short spreads improved over the past week. Historically, after 20-day Multi-Strat gross flows first fell below the 5th percentile (as on Oct. 27), alpha was higher over the next 20 days in 9 of 10 cases.

Broader HF de-grossing may be slowing. US de-grossing is below its seasonal average, and the pattern most resembles the 2022 midterm year, when de-grossing continued into mid-month and gross flows recovered in December alongside a market sell-off with substantial short additions.

HFs rebounded over the following 5 and 10 days in all eight comparable events in the past five years where 5- and 20-day net returns fell below -2z. Earlier examples (late Feb 2020, late Oct 2018) were followed by further losses.

Selling has not signaled broad capitulation. EMEA and China/HK saw net buying while North America and Japan saw net selling, with North America sharply de-grossed. European short covering reached an extreme 3z level, last seen in late 2022.

Exposure has reset: HF net leverage fell about 4% in the past week to near 12-month lows, Eq L/S net leverage is at a three-year low, and global momentum exposure is near three-year lows and close to neutral. Semis were the most net-sold US theme. Software flows are neutral, broader AI-cyclical exposure fell quickly, and Defensives ex-Healthcare have begun to rebound.

tension_points.bull_case: Capitulation signals (largest MOMO unwind in ~40 years, deleveraging at Liberation Day levels), year-end seasonality, short covering rather than chasing, and retail ETF buying support a bounce, with room for risk to be added back.
tension_points.bear_case: Selling has not signaled broad capitulation, North America is sharply de-grossed, and past episodes (Feb 2020, Oct 2018) saw further losses. The 2022 midterm year saw gross flow recovery coincide with a sell-off.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Market conditions deteriorating: a rebound in HF returns depends partly on the market, and the largest US net selling needed for a very negative four-week TPM change has not yet appeared.

tension_points.bull_case: EU earnings fundamentals are good, positioning gives a buy signal, and the geopolitical narrative has improved.
tension_points.bear_case: Macro and thematics favor long US and Asia versus EU, and EU needs stability in EGB spreads. Energy supply is a risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Stability in EGB spreads is needed for EU broadening to gain conviction.
